verification.summary: The only previous mustFix — exporting MOCK_GITHUB_PORT=4000 before invoking spec 001's frozen accs.bash — is gone; both scripts now share the unexported 4123 default and every remaining step lines up with accs.md and the contract.

shouldFix.problem: This whole first half of check_no_dupes builds a block string and pipes it into csplit whose output is never read, discarding files under $OUT/blk* on disk for no purpose. It's dead code that only adds noise and stray files, the real duplicate check is the awk block right after it.

pkill matches by command line, but pnpm spawns a child process (e.g. node dist/index.js) whose argv likely won't contain the literal string 'pnpm mock-github', so this may silently fail to free the port if spec 001's own cleanup trap didn't already do it. Low risk since spec 001's accs.bash should have its own trap-based cleanup, but worth tightening if step 2 ever flakes on 'address in use'.

shouldKnow.problem: The three-arg form of match() capturing into an array is a gawk extension, not POSIX awk. Fine on any normal Linux dev/CI box with gawk as /usr/bin/awk, but would silently misbehave on a system where awk is mawk or BSD awk.

accs.md only specifies the comment body 'Hello World!', not the author; the script picks 'tester' as an unstated default. Reasonable and doesn't affect any check, just wasn't captured in the enriched spec's 'Assumptions taken' list.
